description: For a plain membership question about which drinks are made with or contain a named ingredient, select the ingredient field once before any other lookup. An appended generic type noun yields the distinctive established name ("sencha tea" is sencha); a descriptor that is part of the identity stays ("black tea" stays black tea); neither is bare tea. Blind suffix stripping, synonyms, parallel free-text, stems, varieties, profiles and other ingredients stay out of that selection. The default page size stays unless a page size is specified. That same ingredient and page size continue while another page remains; link every exact returned bottle, and stop after the exact list unless a subset was requested. A missing literal identity allows one check of only that same ingredient's recognizable name, and zero eligible bottles for a resolved identity is a legitimate result. A question that requires additional facts, such as sourcing or brewing, is outside these simple-list instructions. Search published beverages by name, alias or producer name in q, category, exact producer slug, ingredient or preferences, with pagination. A combined producer-plus-product phrase may not match; q does not parse arbitrary sentences. Ingredient matches one exact published name, slug or complete alias, case-insensitively, not a substring. The whole-string fallback from strawberries to strawberry applies only when no published literal identity matches. Ingredient and preferences cannot be combined. Ingredient results are recorded eligible relationships, not complete recipes or every drink in existence. Preferences accept at most 6 unique values: dry, bright, tannic, earthy, smoky and floral. Every requested value requires a current public sensory claim; results cover a bounded candidate window, not the whole catalogue. Dry means an explicit drink-level dry or not-sweet tasting statement, not dried fruit, process, semi-dry, low sugar, acidity, aroma, a name or ABV. Offer-tagged claims are neither proof nor contradiction. Catalogue ABV lacks the source qualifier; null is unknown, not zero. Beyond Wine is a published reference for no/low ABV specialty beverages in fine dining, including wine alternatives, craft ferments, kombucha, teas and blends. It excludes non-alcoholic beer, non-alcoholic spirits, mocktails, mixers, dealcoholized wine and blends containing dealcoholized wine. The connection cannot place orders or take payments and cannot guarantee every drink contains absolutely no alcohol.

category.description: One in-scope category: tea_infusion (Tea Infusion), botanical_infusion (Botanical Infusion), sparkling_tea (Sparkling Tea), fermented_tea (Fermented Tea), juice (Juice), nonfermented_blend (Non-Fermented Blend), fermented_blend (Fermented Blend).

Ingredient and preferences cannot be combined.
